articles.title: EU-länder i ”brådskande” bränslemöte
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: EU-länder i ”brådskande” bränslemöte
articles.body_text: EU:s medlemsländer har kallat till ett brådskande möte i syfte att dämpa de skenande bränslepriserna. Arkivbild. EU:s medlemsstater ska under fredagen träffa EU-kommissionen för att diskutera en gemensam åtgärd mot de skenande bränslepriserna. Det säger en talesperson för kommissionen. Mötet sker i samma veva som USA uppmanar Europa att ”omedelbart” frigöra strategiska dieselreserver i ett försök att hålla nere priserna. ”Våra europeiska partner bör påskynda genomförandet av sina befintliga åtaganden och omedelbart tillgängliggöra ytterligare leveranser för att hantera de pågående störningarna”, skriver finansminister Scott Bessent i ett inlägg på sociala medier. EU:s ansvarige för energifrågor, Dan Jørgensen, förde på torsdagen samtal med bland andra franska, tyska, italienska och brittiska myndigheter för att samordna ländernas ståndpunkter. Dieselmarknaden är för närvarande mycket ansträngd, vilket leder till höga priser för konsumenter över hela världen, säger EU-talespersonen Anna Kaisa Itkonen.

articles.title: Avvaktande på Wall Street
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Avvaktande på Wall Street
articles.body_text: Handlarna på Wall Street har fallande kurser att hantera på torsdagen. Arkivbild. Det var stillastående på börserna i New York i ett läge där marknadsräntorna sjönk tillbaka något medan oljepriset klättrade uppåt igen. Vid stängning var Dow Jones industriindex och tekniktunga Nasdaqs industriindex båda oförändrade medan breda S&P 500 plussade på 0,2 procent. Räntan för tioåriga amerikanska statsobligationer har stigit mycket på kort tid men kyldes ner en aning under dagen, vid 22-tiden låg räntesatsen på 5,24 proncent. Men på oljefronten var utvecklingen det motsatta – sent på torsdagskvällen kostade ett fat Nordsjöolja drygt 102 dollar per fat efter att ha varit nere på 97 dollar i den tidiga handeln.

articles.title: Gigantiskt vindkraftverk ska säkra tysk el
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Gigantiskt vindkraftverk ska säkra tysk el
articles.body_text: Det nytillverkade vindkraftverket sträcker sig 365 meter över marken. Gigantiskt vindkraftverk ska säkra tysk el Med en höjd på 365 meter är det inte bara högre än Eiffeltornet. Tysklands nya vindkraftverk beskrivs nu som världens högsta. Sydost om Berlin, och symboliskt nog tidigare plats för en gruva där brunkol utvanns, har det nya vindkraftverket fått en plats. Det gör sällskap med en rad andra vindkraftssnurror men den här varianten sticker ut i samlingen. Med en höjd på 365 meter når det högt över övriga vindkraftverk och är nästan lika högt som Berlins berömda tv-torn (368 meter). Det är också betydligt högre än exempelvis de allra största svenska motsvarigheterna. I Sverige finns för närvarande tillstånd på vindkraftverk som når en höjd på 290 meter. Förhoppningen är att giganten i Tyskland ska vara i drift från och med i november och bistå till att bidra till landets energiproduktion. Tyskland har under flera års tid försökt att växla om mot förnybar energikällor efter att energipriserna steg kraftigt i anslutning till Rysslands fullskaliga invasion av Ukraina inleddes.

articles.title: Tjänade storkovan på börsen – efter barhänget med advokaten
articles.summary: Drog in hundratusentals kronor • Sex åtalas för grova insiderbrott
articles.body_text: Bild från baren där köpet ska ha diskuterats. Tjänade storkovan på börsen – efter barhänget med advokaten Drog in hundratusentals kronor • Sex åtalas för grova insiderbrott En advokat och fem personer står åtalade för flera fall av insiderhandel i ett forskningsbolag. Enligt åtalet fick flera tips om att bolaget skulle köpas upp på olika utekvällar. De tjänade flera hundratusen kronor när nyheten kom och aktien steg över 200 procent. Den 27 november 2024 träffades två vänner på en bar i centrala Stockholm. Den ene är advokat och var rådgivare inför ett planerat uppköp av ett börsnoterat forskningsbolag. Enligt åklagaren hade advokaten insiderinformation om budet senast den dagen. Under kvällen ansöker vännen om pengar hos Avanza, en kredit som senare används för att köpa aktier. Kvällen därpå söker advokaten på sin mobil efter ”are whatsapp calls really encrypted” och ringer sedan vännen. Dagen efter ses de igen, på en restaurang i Stockholm, och kort därefter börjar vännen köpa aktier. Totalt köper han för 127 199 kronor. Under våren 2025 swishar han advokaten 30 000 kronor, vilket åklagaren menar var betalning för tipset. Han uppger i förhör att han ofta köper aktier, vanligtvis i den här storleken och minns inte förutsättningar för det här köper. Vännen träffar därefter en tredje man. Efter att de setts köper denne aktier för 119 634 kronor och swishar sammanlagt 49 000 kronor till vännen. Enligt förhör fick han ett tips om aktien men uppfattade det som en bra investering, och han vill inte uppge vem tipset kom från. Ytterligare en person som umgåtts med advokaten flyttar 70 000 kronor till sitt Avanzakonto och köper därefter aktier i bolaget för totalt 80 032 kronor. Enligt åklagaren visar mobilpositioneringen att han vid överföringen befann sig hemma hos advokaten. Han swishar advokaten åtta gånger till en sammanlagt summa på 40 000 kronor. Under en utekväll i början av december umgås advokaten med ytterligare två vänner. Efteråt köper de aktier för över hundratusen kronor. Rally i aktien efter nyhet – över 200 procent På kvällen den 15 december tillkännages nyheten om det planerade uppköpet av företaget och aktien steg 206 procent. Enligt åklagarens beräkningar hade de fem som köpte aktier då gjort vinster på mellan cirka 150 000 och drygt 300 000 kronor.

articles.title: Ekonomisk trippelsmällen väntar i vinter
articles.summary: Bränslepriserna höjs redan i dag – och sedan kommer nästa prissmocka
articles.body_text: Trippelsmäll väntar för hushållen: ”Får hoppas på mild vinter” Bränslepriserna höjs redan i dag – och sedan kommer nästa prissmocka De närmaste månaderna väntas en perfekt ekonomisk storm att slå mot Sverige efter att bränslepriserna, räntorna och elpriserna stiger. – Vi får hoppas på en mild vinter, säger chefsekonomen Alexandra Stråberg. Bränslepriserna höjs redan i dag när den första av regeringens tillfälliga sänkningar försvinner. Bensinen går upp med cirka 1,30 kronor per liter och dieseln med 40 öre. Den 1 december löper också sänkningen av koldioxidskatten ut, vilket väntas höja bränslepriserna ytterligare. Samtidigt är det fortsatt oroligt på den globala oljemarknaden, då konflikten i Hormuzsundet mellan USA och Iran fortfarande pågår. – Vi ser att oljepriserna fortfarande är väldigt labila och vi ser ingen lösning än på konflikten. Så priset kan ju bli dyrare även av det skälet, säger Alexandra Stråberg, chefsekonom på Länsförsäkringar. Sverige har näst billigast bensin i EU – endast på Malta är det billigare, enligt nya siffror från EU. I Frankrike, Tyskland och Nederländerna kostar bensinen omkring 26 kronor per liter. Dyrast är bensinen i Danmark. När det gäller diesel placerar sig Sverige mitt i fältet. Återigen är det billigast på Malta och dyrast i Danmark. Inflationen kommer att ligga tydligt över Riksbankens mål nästa år, vilket får negativa effekter för hushåll med bolån. En prognos från Konjukturinstitutet (KI) visar att Riksbanken väntas göra fyra räntehöjningar de kommande två åren, från dagens 1,75 procent till 2,75 procent 2028. För ett hushåll med ett bostadslån på tre miljoner kan det handla om 2500 kronor mer i ränta per månad, på ett år handlar det om 30 000 kronor. Konjukturinstitutet tror däremot inte att inflationen kommer att fortsätta stiga när räntan kommit upp i 2,75 procent. – Nej, inflationen förväntas gå ner och närma sig Riksbankens inflationsmål. Det här är snarare en normalisering av räntan än ett tecken på att nåt är illa i svensk ekonomi, säger Albin Kainelainen, generaldirektör på KI. Däremot kan e n större internationell ränteoro också påverka Sverige. Det skakiga ekonomiska läget är en kombination av fyra olika saker, menar Alexandra Stråberg. Höga statsskulder, höga räntor, budgetundetrskott och ostabilt politiskt läge. – Den kombon är stökig, även om vi inte har den i Sverige. Men vi påverkas såklart av det som sker när kombon finns i andra länder, framför allt i USA, Storbritannien och Frankrike, säger Stråberg. Förutom höjda bränslepriser och höjd marknadsränta kan hushållen få en tredje smäll i vinter: elpriserna. Enligt Energimyndigheten ökar sannolikheten för perioder i vinter med högre elpriser när prisutvecklingen påverkas både av omvärldsläget och av en större andel väderberoende elproduktion. Svängningarna i elpriset väntas också bli större och prisskillnaden kan vara betydande mellan dygnets timmar och mellan olika delar av landet, enligt myndigheten. På frågan om hur mycket man ska oroa sig för elpriset i vinter menar Alexandra Stråberg att det beror på om elproducenterna klarar av trycket. Eftersom priserna på både olja och gas går upp ökar efterfrågan på el.

articles.title: Publicistiska grunden för journalistik på TV4
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4?
articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.title: Bortglömda fiskar
articles.summary: Teatrar och konserthus lockar allt oftare med olika sidoevenemang. Teater Västernorrland har musikquiz, Folkoperan sänder poddar från sin foajé och på Göteborgsoperan kan man höra föredrag eller vara med och dansa. De uppsluppna tillställningarna, före och efter konserter och föreställningar, lockar också en ny sorts publik. En av Östersjöfestivalens mest omtalade programpunkter, förutom musiken i Berwaldhallen, har varit “Bortglömda fiskar” - en oväntad kulinarisk träff med Kålrotsakademin och provsmakning av “svensk sushi”. “Gensvaret från publiken är enormt. Man vill bli överraskad”, konstaterar Emma Nyberg, exekutiv producent på Berwaldhallen. Och på frågan om vad nors och näbbgädda har att göra i ett konserthus kommer det självklara svaret snabbt: “Att äta gott och att lyssna på klassisk musik hör ihop, båda skärper och öppnar våra sinnen.”

articles.title: Putin warns West that Russia is ready to use every weapon to protect Kaliningrad
articles.summary: The Russian leader insists Moscow is "not threatening anyone" and is merely responding to statements by Western leaders.
articles.body_text: Vladimir Putin has said Russia will use all weapons at his disposal if it considers its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad to have come under direct attack. The Russian president insisted that Moscow was "not threatening anyone" and merely responding to statements by Western leaders that it was preparing for war in 2029 or 2030. Throughout this week, Russia has accused Nato of preparing to blockade its territory, which borders Lithuania and Poland, warning that it would even be prepared to use nuclear weapons if the West tried to cut off Kaliningrad from the rest of Russia. Nato has sought to calm the situation, stressing that it was a defensive alliance and urging Moscow to stop its "nuclear threats". Western allies have faced a surge in so-called hybrid warfare incidents blamed on Russia, particularly in Poland and the Baltics in recent months. Last week alone, Poland said a Russian helicopter had strayed into its territory adjacent to Kaliningrad and Lithuania said its population felt "constantly threatened" by Russia, in part because of drones entering the nation's airspace. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Thursday that his country was preparing for further hybrid attacks, "including serious ones", after a drone armed with explosives was found in August on the tarmac at Leipzig airport close to Ukrainian cargo planes. In a wide-ranging speech at the Valdai foreign policy forum, Putin told his audience that he believed that international conflicts were highly likely to continue, but would get better as "Western hegemony" weakened. Although the Russian leader himself began the full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022, he again blamed the West for provoking the invasion, arguing that Moscow had simply been forced to defend itself and take up arms. He also insisted that Russia's attacks on Ukrainian economic targets were a direct response to Ukraine's strikes on Russia's oil refineries and its ships in the Black Sea. "Now from every direction we're receiving calls 'let's stop'. But they started it," he said. Putin admitted Kyiv had "got some results" from its refinery attacks and Russia had lost about 1% of its GDP. Ukraine maintains it began attacking Russian oil infrastructure because it helped the Kremlin finance the war.

articles.title: Renee Good: Family of US woman killed by ICE agent sues Trump officials
articles.summary: Lawyers for Good's family say US officials created "an unprecedented environment for state sponsored violence" in Minneapolis.
articles.body_text: The family of a woman who was killed by an immigration agent in Minneapolis has announced two lawsuits against the US government and members of the Trump administration. Renee Good, a US citizen, was shot to death by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer during a major immigration sweep in January. Millions watched the video recorded of her killing and residents of the Minnesota city took to the streets to protest. One lawsuit blames the government for her death, claiming the operation created "an unprecedented environment for state-sponsored violence", a lawyer for the family said. A White House spokeswoman in a statement called the lawsuits "baseless". The lawsuits were brought by Good's brother, Brent Ganger, and her partner, Becca Good. Speaking publicly for the first time since the shooting, Becca Good told a news conference on the lawsuits on Thursday: "The whole world had to watch as our entire universe was destroyed." "We were all robbed," she said as she described how the shooting affected their three children. In one of the lawsuits, the family accuses the government of "battery, assault, false imprisonment, intentional infliction of emotional distress and negligence that caused Renee's death", according to the family's lawyer. It cites the Federal Tort Claims Act, which allows citizens to sue the government for personal injury, death or property damage caused by the negligence of federal employees. The second lawsuit targets ICE officer Jonathan Ross, who shot Good, as well as White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, White House border tsar Tom Homan and others, alleging a "conspiracy to interfere with civil rights by senior federal officials, federal immigration enforcement agents and private actors". "Our government has become a grave and mortal threat to its own citizens," the family's lawyer, Antonio Romanucci told Thursday's news conference. In her statement, Lauren Bis, a spokeswoman for the White House, said the deaths of Americans at the hands of illegal immigrants should merit "equal coverage" by news media.

articles.title: Fires break out at French schools as students protest nationwide
articles.summary: The French government holds a crisis meeting as demonstrations grow and become violent in places.
articles.body_text: Fires have broken out at several schools in France, as students protest by blockading education institutions nationwide over school funding and studying conditions. Blazes were reported at two high schools in Nantes, western France, while another was filmed engulfing the entrance of a school in the northern city of Rouen. Students are protesting about a lack of teachers and staff, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings. University students joined the demonstrations on Thursday, citing similar demands. The interior ministry said 1,949 people had been arrested on Thursday, with 305 police officers injured. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu held a crisis meeting on Thursday to discuss the unrest. The government said afterwards that the student-led demonstrations had descended into "urban violence". Both fires in Nantes spread after a bin was set alight. The blaze at the Nelson Mandela high school, in the city centre, then spread to the front of the building, damaging the entrance hall. In the southern city of Marseille, staff at Victor Hugo high school were splashed with petrol as protesters reportedly filled containers. While in the north, a headteacher at Degrugillier high school, in the village of Auchel, was injured in the ear by a wayward firework. The blockades and protests at French lycées - for 15-18 year olds and equivalent to sixth forms in the UK or high schools in the US - began last week before spreading to hundreds of schools across the country. So far, 1,027 lycees have been affected by demonstrations, with blockades at 222 of them, according to the interior ministry. At least 30 universities have also reportedly been blockaded, including campuses in Rennes and Paris. On Thursday, public transport services in Marseille and Strasbourg were halted due vandalism, threats of violence and to hinder protesters from moving around.

articles.title: Algeria introduces death penalty for arsonists after wildfires
articles.summary: It is estimated more than 200 people have died in blazes in the north-east of the country over the summer.
articles.body_text: Algeria has adopted a law imposing the death penalty on people convicted of arson of forests or fields after a series of deadly wildfires swept parts of the country. Members of the national assembly voted through the bill, which also made child abduction a capital offence, on Thursday. Capital punishment has been in the country's penal code for some offences, but no execution has been carried out since 1993. The official death toll from the blazes stands at 12, but independent news outlets believe the figure to be much higher. Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune ordered the justice ministry to introduce the changes to the criminal law after more than 100 fires in the north-east of the country during an intense heatwave in northern Africa. Under the law, anyone convicted of deliberately setting fire to forests, woods or fields could face execution. The death penalty has also been extended to child kidnappings that involve torture, sexual assault or mutilation. According to news agency AFP, Justice Minister Lotfi Boudjemaa told parliament: "The adoption of the death penalty for these acts is the appropriate legal response to curb these crimes." The tougher penalties were justified because arson had reached "the level of organised crime", with investigations suggesting links to "foreign parties", Boudjemaa said. The upper house, the Council of the Nation, will review the law before it is officially ratified by the president. Investigative journalist Nozha Khelalef has been gathering the names of those believed to have died in the fires from death notices posted by families and information shared by some local authorities. Her tally, listed on the independent news website Twala , puts the death toll at 200.

articles.title: Christa Pike in critical condition after surviving two lethal injections, lawyer says
articles.summary: Pike’s lawyers have asked for her death sentence to be commuted following the botched execution.
articles.body_text: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike is in "critical condition, receiving life-saving care" at hospital, after surviving two lethal injection attempts, leading the state's governor to halt all executions for the year. "We don't have a sense of her prognosis or much update on her health at the moment," her lawyer Randy Spivey told reporters on Thursday. "But we do know that that she is alive right now." Her lawyers are now asking for her sentence to be commuted. Pike, 50, was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer. She was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital on Wednesday but remained alive, her lawyers said. She was then sent to hospital in an ambulance. Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer. Her attempted execution on Wednesday was the subject of a last-minute legal battle. This culminated in the US Supreme Court allowing the lethal injections to go ahead. Slemmer's mother May Martinez, who was among those who wanted the execution to take place and who travelled to Tennessee to witness it, told NBC News after the botched attempt that "it was a mess". On Thursday afternoon, Pike's lawyers offered more details about what happened during the attempted execution, describing a harrowing scene shrouded in secrecy. "Last night, the execution team attempted to establish an IV line for an hour," Spivey said. "I counted at least seven needles used in her left arm alone, one of which appeared to be bent when it was pulled from her arm after an unsuccessful attempt." Spivey said that observers were kept in a dark room behind a closed curtain, after the second lethal dose had been administered and "it was clear that Miss Pike was still breathing" minutes later. "No one knew what was going on behind that curtain," Spivey said. "I had no idea when and if medical professionals began to assist." Spivey said the state's governor must commute Christa's sentence now, a request that was denied previously.

articles.title: Flydubai attacker 'underwent Islamist radical indoctrination', Netanyahu says
articles.summary: Israel's prime minister says the pilot who tried to take over the Flydubai plane clearly intended to "down the plane".
articles.body_text: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says investigations suggest the man who stabbed his fellow pilot and tried to take over a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination". The Flydubai plane plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) two hours into its journey on Wednesday, before passengers and crew overpowered the attacker and retook control to land safely. Netanyahu told Fox News that it was looking "very likely" that the attacker, who he said was an Omani national, "was going to down the plane". Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) state news agency reports investigations have begun there to determine "whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose". The Interior Ministry of Saudi Arabia - where the plane made an emergency landing - said that both the pilot and co-pilot had been sent back to the UAE on Thursday morning after medical teams had cleared them. UAE officials earlier claimed jurisdiction over the incident because the aircraft on which the attack took place is registered there and flies under its flag. Netanyahu told Fox that once the attacker had been subdued and tied up by passengers and crew, he was "calling out to the aircrew 'kill me, kill me', so it's clear he was suicidal - that's not a question". "And with all the passengers in there, and if you couple that with what I just told you about the Islamist tendencies, that radicalisation that were found in his background, I think... that'll give us a pretty good clue." However, he stressed that he did not want to draw any firm conclusions as to motive yet. Both US President Donald Trump and UAE officials have indicated to the media that Iran may be responsible for the incident, without definitively blaming Tehran. Trump told reporters on Thursday that Iran would be "hit very hard" if it was deemed to have been involved in the attack. Pilots from countries without diplomatic relations with Israel were usually not allowed to fly there, Netanyahu said when asked about how the suspected Omani pilot came to be on the plane.

articles.title: Russian dissident Garry Kasparov says US warned him of danger to his life
articles.summary: "My family and I will not truly be safe as long as Putin is in power," says the former chess world champion.
articles.body_text: An exiled Russian opposition figure living in the US says he was warned by American and Lithuanian security services that his life was in danger. Former chess world champion Garry Kasparov said he was one of two dissidents told to take precautions, which he had done. His comments come after the US Justice Department unsealed an indictment earlier this month charging five people who allegedly work for a network linked to the Kremlin with plotting attacks and murders in countries including the US, focusing on Russian dissidents and defectors. Kasparov wrote in his publication The Next Move that he had not been told explicitly that he and fellow Free Russia Forum co-founder Ivan Tyutrin were considered targets, but said both had been warned about their safety. Spanish newspaper El Mundo reported that it had obtained information that Kasparov, along with another Russian opposition figure, Ilya Ponomarev, had been warned about the plot over the summer by US authorities. Citing sources close to Kasparov, the paper said he had been placed under enhanced protection over the summer for the first time since he moved to the US. Kasparov wrote separately: "I will not stop and I will not hide, even if I thought it was possible to do so. "My family and I will not truly be safe as long as [Russian President Vladimir] Putin is in power in Russia - a circumstance shared by millions." Kasparov retired from competitive chess in 2005 to pursue a career in politics, founding movements that openly opposed Putin before fleeing Russia in 2013. He has not returned since. Russia classed him as a foreign agent following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and subsequently added him to a list of terrorists and extremists in 2024 - both categorisations he rejects. The other reported target, Ponomarev, was the only Russian MP who voted against the illegal annexation of Crimea in 2014 and later went into exile in Ukraine. He declined to confirm or deny to the Moscow Times whether he had been tipped off about the alleged plot but said the allegations marked "a new level of escalation" by Russia.

articles.title: Flydubai passenger describes hugging his children as plane nosedived during attack
articles.summary: Adam Polovincik tells the BBC he told his young children "everything is going to be all right" as flight plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m).
articles.body_text: A man has described how he hugged and reassured his two young children as their plane suddenly descended after one pilot stabbed the other in an attempt to seize control of the flight. A Flydubai plane plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) in less than two minutes around two hours into its journey from Dubai to Tel Aviv on Wednesday, before passengers and crew overpowered him and retook control to land safely. Adam Polovincik told BBC Newshour that he hugged his six-year-old son and three-year-old daughter "really hard" and tried to stay calm for them as the attack unfolded. He praised the pilot who was stabbed and passengers who fought off and subdued the attacker, saying they were "true heroes". The stabbed pilot is in a stable condition in hospital, while the alleged attacker has been arrested. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said it was too early to say whether Iran was involved in the attack , but that the alleged attacker had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination". Polovincik, who was sitting in aisle 13, was flying home with his wife and children after an "amazing" holiday in Singapore and Thailand. He said there had been a "huge degree of panic" on the plane as there was a "very, very, very sharp decrease in height". He thought at first that this was simply because of an air pocket, but "it took a lot of time, almost a minute". Everyone who had not been seated fell to the floor, the 40-year-old said. "After a couple of seconds, we started to hear screams. 'There is blood, there is stabbing, we need help'," Polovincik said. "At the end of the day, you understand very, very quickly that literally there is nothing that you can do at this point in time," he said.

articles.title: Kanye West's Russia shows cancelled after stadium row
articles.summary: Chaos has surrounded the St Petersburg shows since the stadium said it had not agreed to host the rapper.
articles.body_text: Two stadium gigs in Russia by Ye, the rapper formerly known as Kanye West, have officially been cancelled. West had been due to perform at the Gazprom Arena in St Petersburg on 10 and 11 October. But there was confusion in the lead-up to the shows, as the venue had said it wouldn't host him for what would have been the biggest show by a western artist since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. In a post on messaging app Telegram, gig organisers Say Agency confirmed the concerts had been cancelled with "sincere regret". "The Ye concerts in St Petersburg will not be able to take place on the scheduled dates," the Moscow-based agency wrote. "We will issue an official statement regarding the status of the project and our plans in the near future." Gazprom Arena said in August that it had not signed a rental agreement with the concert promoters and so the gig could not take place on its site. Say Agency had said it was working to resolve the issue with the stadium before confirming they could not go ahead. The stadium also acknowledged it had received complaints about West's performance. He has recently apologised for multiple antisemitic and pro-Nazi comments in the past, saying he had "lost touch with reality" as a result of his bipolar disorder. Russia was invaded by the Nazis in World War Two, and the country's Foreign Ministry spokeswoman was among those who criticised the planned shows. Maria Zakharova said they were unacceptable and pointed out West's "glorification" of Hitler.

articles.title: Trump's AI rebrand causes 'unprecedented' demand for Slovenian website names
articles.summary: The president wants AI to be called super intelligence - or SI - the same initials used by Slovenian domains.
articles.body_text: Donald Trump's push to rename AI may be behind an "unprecedented" rise in registrations for domain names in Slovenia, according to its official national registry. The US president wants AI to be called "super intelligence" - or SI - the same initials used by Slovenian websites. Register.si spokeswoman Klara Herman said 44,000 web addresses with the .si suffix had been registered in September, compared to less than 2,000 in August - an increase of more than 2,100%. She said the scale of activity in late September was "unprecedented" compared to the previous 12 months. Trump called for the technology to be renamed during his speech to the United Nations General Assembly in New York on 11 September. "The use of the word artificial makes it sound fake," he said. "It's not fake, it's actually amazing. But we have to be careful... welcome to the new world of super intelligence." Internet domains are the unique human-readable addresses people type into their web browsers to access websites - like bbc.co.uk. Herman said registrations for .si web addresses in September stood out "very clearly" against the other months in the year, although she was "cautious" about attributing the entire increase to just Trump's comments. She said on 30 September alone, 11,000 new registrations were recorded. One possible explanation for the purchases is a practice in which people speculatively register specific domain names in case they increase in value later on and can be sold for a profit. For example, in 1997 Rick Schwartz, known as "The Domain King", bought the domain name men.com for $15,000 (£11,300). He sold it for $1.32 million seven years later.

articles.title: What happened in the failed execution of Christa Pike - and what next?
articles.summary: The convicted killer is in hospital in Tennessee after surviving two lethal injections, in a case that has raised many questions.
articles.body_text: US convicted murderer Christa Pike is in a critical condition in hospital after Tennessee authorities failed to execute her by lethal injection, her lawyer says. The case of Pike, whose attempted execution on Wednesday had already been the subject of a high-profile legal battle, has raised a number of questions. These include what went wrong, what happens next, and - for opponents of the death penalty - fresh concerns around the suffering of an inmate when an execution does not go to plan. A review into what happened has been ordered and executions in Tennessee have been halted for the rest of the year, Governor Bill Lee said. Pike, 50, was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, an attack that carried out alongside her then-boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp, who was 17. Shipp remains in prison, having been spared the death penalty under state law. Pike was scheduled to be put to death in Tennessee on Wednesday evening local time. The injections were allowed by the Supreme Court at the eleventh hour after the legal battle. Pike was given two injections of the drug pentobarbital but her legal team said these failed to stop her heartbeat and that she could still be heard snoring. The Tennessee Department of Correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out." The state protocol does not clearly specify what should happen if an inmate remains alive after a second dose, according to the AP news agency. Authorities are yet to say whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have yet to give their explanation of why the dosage given to Pike was non-fatal, although medical experts have given theories. Dr Joel Zivot, a professor at the Emory University School of Medicine, told the BBC Pike probably never achieved a sufficient blood level of pentobarbital to cause her breath to stop or heart failure. The Tennessee correction department said Pike had been taken to an off-site medical facility, while one of her lawyers said on Wednesday that she was being given "life-saving measures" in hospital.

articles.title: Captain Smit Machchhar: The 'hero' India pilot who was stabbed on Israel-bound flight
articles.summary: Capt Smit Machchhar was attacked by another pilot onboard the Flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv.
articles.body_text: The pilot who was stabbed on an Israel-bound flight on Wednesday has been identified as Indian national Capt Smit Machchhar. Machchhar was attacked by another pilot onboard a Flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv, forcing the plane to divert to Saudi Arabia. The captain, who has been hailed as a "true hero" by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, was taken to a hospital in Tabuk, a city in north-western Saudi Arabia. The Indian embassy in the United Arab Emirates said Machchhar was "in good health and recovering well". Ambassador Deepak Mittal said he was "proud of Capt Smit for his bravery" and "very reassured" to meet him. Netanyahu wrote on X that Machchhar "saved the lives of 174 people" and prevented "a catastrophic mid-air disaster". Machchhar grew up in the Indian city of Mumbai, where his parents still live. In 2008, he joined Mainland Air, an aviation college in New Zealand's Dunedin, before joining Indian airline SpiceJet as a commercial pilot three years later. He moved to Dubai and joined Flydubai in 2022 as an experienced pilot. Philip Kean, the CEO of Mainland Air, told the BBC he remembered Machchhar as a man who would remain calm in a crisis. "We trained him for forced landing - not this kind of situation, which is very, very rare," Kean said. "It was a long time back but he came across as a good and honest worker." Machchhar has more than 9,750 hours of flying experience, including more than 6,400 hours as pilot-in-command, according to his LinkedIn profile. His former employer SpiceJet issued a statement calling Machchhar a "hero" who had saved "countless lives". An old friend who worked with him at SpiceJet, Capt Dharav Gosalia, described him as outgoing and "very jovial" .

articles.title: Song Min-ho: K-pop star convicted of violating military service law
articles.summary: The member of K-pop band Winner was given a suspended prison sentence for repeated absences from his national service work.
articles.body_text: A South Korean court has handed a suspended one-year prison sentence to K-pop singer Song Min-ho after he was convicted of violating the country's military service law. The 33-year-old member of the boy band Winner was found to have been absent multiple times at a community centre in Seoul, where he had worked as a social worker from 2023 to 2024. All able-bodied men in South Korea have to serve at least 18 months in the military. But some are alternatively assigned as social service personnel for health reasons. The prison sentence handed on Thursday is suspended for two years. That means he can avoid incarceration if he does not commit any crime during that two-year probationary period. The court heard that Song, who is also known by his stage name Mino, had recorded 102 unauthorised absences during his 21-month stint as a social service agent. Military service is a duty to be performed "faithfully", and social service agents are "no exception", the court said. But the court also noted that Song had admitted to the charges and shown remorse. Authorities launched an investigation into Song shortly after he was discharged in 2024, when local media reported that he was frequently absent from his social service duties and took excessive sick leave. Song's supervisor at the social service centre was also given a suspended jail sentence for helping him dodge his duties, including falsifying records to make it look like Song had reported to work. The conscription of South Korea's entertainers has long been a topic of national public debate. Gangnam Style singer Psy famously had to enlist twice, once in 2003 and another time in 2007, after a Seoul court ruled that he had neglected his duties by continuing his showbiz activities during his first national service stint. Steve Yoo, one of the country's biggest pop stars in the 1990s and early 2000s, was embroiled in a national scandal after he was found to have evaded military service in 2002. South Korean authorities banned him from the country after he renounced his citizenship and became a US national shortly before he was due to serve in the military.

articles.title: Japan raises permanent residency fees for foreigners by 20 times
articles.summary: The hikes are part of immigration policy changes introduced to manage Japan's growing foreign population.
articles.body_text: Japan has raised fees for foreigners seeking permanent residency in the country by 20 times to 200,000 yen ($1,270; £955). Those seeking permanent residency must now also meet new income, pension and Japanese-language requirements. Long lines formed outside immigration offices earlier this week as applicants sought to beat the fee hikes, with Tokyo's main immigration bureau reporting wait times of over seven hours. The fee increases are part of a series of changes to Japan's immigration policy under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, which aim to manage its rapidly growing foreign population. In July, Japan implemented a five-fold increase in visa fees for all foreigners – its first visa fee hike in 50 years. Authorities said this was meant to "reflect inflation and exchange rate fluctuations". Although immigration remains politically sensitive and restrictive in Japan, the nation's ageing population is increasingly relying on foreign workers to plug a labour shortage. Japan's foreign resident population surpassed 4.12 million at the end of 2025, marking a record 9.5% increase from the previous year. This however has led to growing anxieties over immigration and social change. Takaichi has made managing immigration one of her key priorities since she took office in October last year. In an X post days before the residency permit hikes set in, Takaichi wrote that her government recognises that "some members of the public may feel a sense of concern or unfairness" as Japan's foreign resident population grows. "To address these concerns, [the government] is working to ensure that its policies toward foreign nationals are orderly, and that both Japanese citizens and foreign residents can live safely and securely," she wrote. Before the hikes, it would cost non-permanent residents in Japan 6,000 yen each time they applied to change their residency status or extend their period of stay. From 1 October, the fee varies according to the duration of stay sought – from 10,000 yen for three months or less, to 75,000 yen for five years or more.

articles.title: Perú Sub 20 Odesur: el bronce es una buena noticia pero ahora, ¿cuál es la gran tarea de los clubes?
articles.summary: La selección peruana Sub 20, con gol de Cari y autogol de Orellana, consiguió el bronce en los Odesur tras vencer 2-1 a Chile y dejó una noticia que el fútbol peruano necesitaba. Pero el verdadero desafío empieza ahora: acompañar a estos jóvenes y exigir a los clubes que les den real competencia
articles.body_text: Más que ilusión, efímera y por eso mismo impredecible, la selección peruana Sub 20 que acaba de obtener el bronce en los Odesur, me provoca alegría. El rostro de los muchachos, una cierta paz. Hecho de retazos, con clubes en ruinas y una Liga 1 que se juega también en los juzgados, el fútbol peruano tiene por fin una buena noticia. Fue 2-1 sobre Chile, contra quien no hay que jugar, solo ganar. Y aunque somos -mea culpa- usualmente ingratos con ellos, pocas veces cubrimos sus entrenamientos, no entendemos los procesos y mucho menos las carencias y, sobre todo, les pedimos respuestas de adultos cuando apenas han terminado el colegio, su optimismo es tan colectivo que en su mesa de festejos hay sitio para todos. No alcanza, sin embargo, con felicitarlos y publicar sus fotos radiantes. Hace falta acompañarlos -la verdadera prueba de fuego es el Sub 20 de enero- y exigir: es escalofriante que ningún jugador de esta selección sea titular en un equipo de Primera -ni siquiera la figura del equipo, Piero Cari, olvidado en Matute-, y que solo sea Sporting Cristal quien realmente proteja una política de exposición y crecimiento de su cantera: Jair Moretti, Josémaría Mellan -la personalidad que tiene-, Duham Ballumbrosio o Gerson Castillo, cuatro megatitulares del equipo de Thiago Kosloski, tienen minutos en la Liga 1 y, en su postura, su juego, su físico, se nota. La Sub 17 de Oré, los medallistas de Nanjing y ahora ellos. Tres buenas campañas de menores en veinte años no alcanza y no alcanzará si se repiten los mismos errores: clubes de corto plazo, dirigentes débiles y reporteros que nos metemos hasta su desayuno. Bastante sólido en defensa, solidario en el medio y quizá demasiado cuidadoso contra rivales que se presentan superiores -el partido contra Argentina de semis- el equipo peruano se suma a la legión de ganadores de estos Odesur. Que la alegría dure hoy y mañana todo sea triple exigencia. Sobre todo para los ciegos clubes.

articles.summary: Este lunes 28 de septiembre desde las 3:45 p.m., Keiko Fujimori, presidenta del Perú, realizará un anuncio en materia laboral en una ceremonia que se llevará a cabo en Palacio de Gobierno.
articles.body_text: Este lunes 28 de septiembre desde las 3:45 p.m., Keiko Fujimori, presidenta del Perú, realizará un anuncio en materia laboral en una ceremonia que se llevará a cabo en Palacio de Gobierno. Uno de los puntos que la mandataria abordará será la aprobación del primer tramo del sueldo mínimo. Como se recuerda, Fujimori anunció el incremento de la Remuneración Mínima Vital (RMV) a S/1.300. La mandataria estará acompañada de Luis Galarreta, presidente del Consejo de Ministros. Además, la ceremonia contará con la participación de Juan Sheput, ministro de Trabajo y Promoción del Empleo y el titular del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Elmer Cuba. Cabe señalar que el ministro de Trabajo, Juan Sheput, sostuvo que el primer alza de la RMV, de unos S/100, se aplicaría entre octubre y noviembre de este año, mientras que el segundo incremento, de S/70, en el siguiente semestre.

articles.title: Perú Sub 20 Odesur: el bronce es una buena noticia pero ahora, ¿cuál es la gran tarea de los clubes?
articles.summary: La selección peruana Sub 20, con gol de Cari y autogol de Orellana, consiguió el bronce en los Odesur tras vencer 2-1 a Chile y dejó una noticia que el fútbol peruano necesitaba. Pero el verdadero desafío empieza ahora: acompañar a estos jóvenes y exigir a los clubes que les den real competencia
articles.body_text: Más que ilusión, efímera y por eso mismo impredecible, la selección peruana Sub 20 que acaba de obtener el bronce en los Odesur, me provoca alegría. El rostro de los muchachos, una cierta paz. Hecho de retazos, con clubes en ruinas y una Liga 1 que se juega también en los juzgados, el fútbol peruano tiene por fin una buena noticia. Fue 2-1 sobre Chile, contra quien no hay que jugar, solo ganar. Y aunque somos -mea culpa- usualmente ingratos con ellos, pocas veces cubrimos sus entrenamientos, no entendemos los procesos y mucho menos las carencias y, sobre todo, les pedimos respuestas de adultos cuando apenas han terminado el colegio, su optimismo es tan colectivo que en su mesa de festejos hay sitio para todos. No alcanza, sin embargo, con felicitarlos y publicar sus fotos radiantes. Hace falta acompañarlos -la verdadera prueba de fuego es el Sub 20 de enero- y exigir: es escalofriante que ningún jugador de esta selección sea titular en un equipo de Primera -ni siquiera la figura del equipo, Piero Cari, olvidado en Matute-, y que solo sea Sporting Cristal quien realmente proteja una política de exposición y crecimiento de su cantera: Jair Moretti, Josémaría Mellan -la personalidad que tiene-, Duham Ballumbrosio o Gerson Castillo, cuatro megatitulares del equipo de Thiago Kosloski, tienen minutos en la Liga 1 y, en su postura, su juego, su físico, se nota. La Sub 17 de Oré, los medallistas de Nanjing y ahora ellos. Tres buenas campañas de menores en veinte años no alcanza y no alcanzará si se repiten los mismos errores: clubes de corto plazo, dirigentes débiles y reporteros que nos metemos hasta su desayuno. Bastante sólido en defensa, solidario en el medio y quizá demasiado cuidadoso contra rivales que se presentan superiores -el partido contra Argentina de semis- el equipo peruano se suma a la legión de ganadores de estos Odesur. Que la alegría dure hoy y mañana todo sea triple exigencia. Sobre todo para los ciegos clubes.

articles.title: One year later, Tesla and Musk still don't have a good definition of 'abundance' | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The CEO promised to get more specific about his vision. But the details are still absent.
articles.body_text: On September 1, 2025, Elon Musk laid out his fourth “ Master Plan ” for Tesla, which was immediately criticized by some of his most ardent fans for being generic . Musk agreed and promised to add more specifics. They never came. But that hasn’t stopped Musk and other Tesla executives from spending much of the past year promising that the company’s many futuristic efforts — robotaxis, robots, AI — are all part of a grander machine that will create an era of “amazing abundance.” What that means, more than a year later, is still tricky to pin down. The topline promises of the plan have remained big and bawdy even as its tagline has changed from sustainable abundance — a clearer connection to the company’s former mission — to the “amazing abundance” slogan, which Musk chose because it was “more joyful.” Musk has talked about a far-flung future where robots and AI do surgery and increase access to medical care. He has said the proliferation of AI and robotics means that “everyone can have a penthouse if they want.” He (virtually) shouted “Amazing abundance for all!” in a quote-tweet of a post from Midjourney founder David Holz, who had claimed 5 million humanoid robots could “build Manhattan in ~6 months.” In July, Musk told Economist editor-in-chief Zanny Minton Beddoes that amazing abundance means “anyone can have anything they can think of.” He also mentioned on Joe Rogan’s podcast late last year that “sustainable abundance” would mean “we haven’t destroyed nature” or “paved the rainforest” and we still “have the national parks,” despite supporting two politicians — Donald Trump and Jair Bolsonaro — who have actively worked against those goals. He appears to have only made this particular claim once, though. Practical details are basically nonexistent, though. Does Musk really think that people want to build three billion nearly-empty apartment buildings with an average of two to three tenants to each lone penthouse? He doesn’t say. Tesla and Musk didn’t respond to requests for comment. While some of these ideas sound like the kind of proclamations uttered after a hearty bong rip in freshman housing, Tesla hasn’t treated them as frivolous. Quite the opposite: Master Plan IV became a central justification for handing Musk a $1 trillion pay package in 2025. Tesla has said in regulatory filings that the “product goals” in that comp package — 20 million vehicles delivered, 10 million active subscriptions to Full Self-Driving, and deploying one million each of its robotaxis and robots — play a “key role” in supporting Musk’s “vision” of abundance. Tesla’s chair Robyn Denholm called this out in a letter to shareholders after they approved the $1 trillion plan last November. “[Y]ou support the vision embodied by Master Plan Part IV and want us to keep steering Tesla toward the extraordinary future we all see ahead,” Denholm wrote. “A world that is not ‘zero-sum’ but instead one in which we can and will accelerate global prosperity for all by creating a safer, cleaner and more enjoyable world. In a year when many tried to sow doubt and negativity, you chose a better future.”

articles.body_text: Airbnb rolled out its new AI-powered search this week as part of its fall update, a significant step for a company that has been slow and deliberate about AI. Co-founder and CEO Brian Chesky has said in the past that a chatbot-only interface is not fit for travel discovery . With more AI on the way to the Airbnb app, I caught up with Chesky over Zoom to talk about how the company is approaching it, where interfaces are headed, why consumer AI still isn’t working, and what role voice will play. Chesky hasn’t changed his mind on chatbots. He said they aren’t good for browsing or shopping because they give you a few options at a time, and you have to take multiple turns before reaching a result. But he doesn’t see the current version of Airbnb’s search as the final form either: its interface will evolve over time. “I think that I’ve believed for a long time that a chatbot isn’t the right interface for e-commerce. I think what you’re seeing today is also not the endgame for e-commerce or for travel or shopping. I think that there’s going to be some interface that is, you know, I don’t want to call it a midpoint, but something between a chatbot and what you see in the first version we shipped,” he said. Continued Chesky: “You know, a lot of people want some things … to be fast and easy, like ‘Book me a flight, I don’t want to look at it.’ With Airbnb, they enjoy looking at the product. Travel studies show that people actually derive more pleasure in planning and anticipating travel than they do traveling. So you don’t want to take the inspiration and the browsing and the library experience of dreaming away.” Chesky sees a second problem with chatbots, which is that they are built for one person. He feels that they aren’t a collaborative interface, which matters for a product that people often use with family and friends. Over the next three to six months, the company’s task is to explore interfaces that enable “multiplayer” AI, meaning AI that several people, such as a group planning a trip together, can use at once. Airbnb isn’t the only one rethinking what an AI interface should look like. As AI tools evolve, new interfaces are also showing up in apps. Startups like Monogram and, more recently, Wabi are experimenting with “generative” interfaces, which are screens an AI builds on-the-fly rather than ones a designer fixed in advance. Chesky thinks people will see a mix of deterministic (pre-designed and predictable) and generative interfaces. I asked Chesky how Airbnb is preparing for consumer AI agents, which are tools like Instinct and Muse that carry out tasks on a person’s behalf. Agents will need robust software infrastructure on Airbnb’s end, he said, and the company wants to make itself more agent-friendly. In his view, they could be good lead generators. “I don’t necessarily know if I believe in a world that there’s apps in the future, but I don’t believe in a world where the apps become data layers of a universal simple UI because when you open your iPhone, there is a reason Airbnb’s app is a different design than DoorDash, Shopify, and Amazon. Our interfaces should be adaptive to the utility and the function that we’re doing. We want to make our app more agentic, and we want to build a lot more user interface controls,” he said. “If I have an agent, but I also want like really great browse functionality, if I want to be able to message the host like an Airbnb, if I want to be able to compare, if I want to be able to verify my identity, if I want to be able to use a map feature, if I want to then be able to add other items, then if I want to stay in the platform, then either the agent has to do a handoff or the agent application would need to build a bit more of, I think, a robust software developer kit to bring the app to you, so to speak.” Chesky thinks that there were concerns around AI tools cutting companies like Airbnb out of the customer relationship, but he said that chatbots have proven to be good at lead generation. The Airbnb CEO is also planning for agent-to-agent interactions through the platform. He explained there might be some interactions within the platform and some with agents of other apps. His thesis is that apps have not always been interoperable unless companies struck a business deal. On the other hand, agents are like “apps with faces,” and when they talk to each other, all apps can become interoperable. “I think of the Airbnb app as one day becoming an agent, you know, where basically the explore tab has an agent, our customer service has an agent, we’re developing another agent in another service area. Probably eventually there’s going to be a macro Airbnb agent. And that will probably be interoperable with MCP [a standard that lets AI agents connect with other software] to other agents,” Chesky noted.

articles.title: Photon held a funeral for mobile apps. Now it has $4.5M to help replace them with agents. | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The startup helps developers build AI agents that work over iMessage, SMS/RCS, email, and other messaging platforms. It's a bet that consumers will increasingly use agents instead of downloading apps.
articles.body_text: The AI startup Photon is so sure that agents will eventually come to replace mobile apps that it held a funeral for the latter — yes, a real funeral in a church, with speeches and everything. Photon, which helps developers build agents that work over iMessage and WhatsApp, now has $4.5 million in seed funding to develop its products. The raise comes after the company signed up over 40,000 developers and grew its revenue 10x in just four months, it says. Photon co-founder and CEO Daniel Tian said the “ app funeral ,” held in San Francisco on September 17, was also a developer day for the startup, featuring panels from Vercel, Stripe, and OpenAI. It also included an actual coffin for app icons. The move to host an app funeral was obviously somewhat tongue-in-cheek, but Tian believes the app era is coming to an end. “Honestly, it’s going to take a while, but I think, directionally, it’s inevitable,” he said of the shift from apps to agents. The thesis behind the startup, as you may have guessed, is that users no longer want to install new apps. Instead, they want access to agents that work through the messaging apps they already use, like iMessage and WhatsApp. Meta’s Muse, whose app has soared to No. 1 on the app stores, is putting that theory to the test. But even if Muse comes to dominate the consumer AI space, Tian sees a market for serving developers who want their applications to work over messaging services. That’s why Photon is offering a package of tools, including a unified API, an extensible channel framework, a command-line interface (CLI), and an observability suite. Combined, they allow developers to build and operate an agent experience that works over iMessage, WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS or RCS, email, voice, and more. The idea for Photon emerged from the time co-founders Tian and Ryan Zhu, the CTO, spent building consumer apps as students, often at hackathons. Every time they finished a new app, they hit the same bottleneck: getting people to discover it. By building an agent that worked within iMessage, they realized they could reach people through an app those people already use every day: Apple’s Messages. Tian, for instance, had built a bot that would text his friends back as him over iMessage. When he and Zhu made the technology open source on GitHub, thousands of developers adopted it. So they went all in. Tian dropped out of UPenn’s M&T program, and Zhu left high school, later becoming a visiting student at MIT’s Media Lab. Today, the open source version of Photon still accounts for 98% of its use. This April, the founders decided to create a managed platform and sell access to it via subscription tiers. This hosted version of the product offers 99.95% uptime, which is much higher than what you’d get if you were just running the open source version on your local Mac for a hobby project. It’s also SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA-compliant, which opens the door to healthcare agent use cases. To date, the startup’s platform has attracted over 40,000 developer sign-ups and now includes paying clients. (Any usage beyond 10 users requires moving out of the free tier to one of the three paid tiers, we’re told.) The company isn’t sharing revenue figures but said that, in addition to the 10x revenue growth, it’s seeing less than 3% churn, and its messaging volume has grown by 5x in the last month alone. Customers using Photon include Corgi Insurance; social introductions app Boardy; Gen Z dating platform Ditto; business banking platform Rho; finance AI assistant Fliptexts; AI email client Slashy; and others building agents for fintech, consumer AI, and other vertical use cases. Photon’s technology integration partners also include companies such as Vercel (Eve and ChatSDK) and Nous Research, whose Hermes agent uses Photon as its default iMessage layer. Photon is also the layer under Tencent’s QClaw and NanoClaw. Plus, Photon has seen framework and infra integrations across LangChain, Mastra, Convex, Render, Railway, and Telnyx, among others.

articles.title: The new Kindle ditches the raised bezel in a push toward a smaller, lighter e-reader | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The new Kindle lineup features its lightest and thinnest designs yet, with a sleek, front-flush display that eliminates bezels for good.
articles.body_text: Amazon is giving the Kindle its most significant physical redesign in years, introducing a refreshed lineup of e-readers built around a deceptively simple idea: getting rid of the raised bezel. The redesigned Kindle unveiled Thursday replaces the traditional raised bezel surrounding the display with a flush-front design, creating a cleaner, more seamless look. But bezels also give readers a place to rest their fingers without accidentally touching the screen and triggering a page turn or another touchscreen command. Amazon says it has designed around that problem. At a press briefing, Kevin Keith, Amazon’s vice president of devices, said the company is using “Cap” (capacitive) touch technology and haptics to create what he describes as a “dead zone.” As a reader grips the Kindle, the device detects where a finger is resting and adjusts the touch-sensitive area accordingly. “When you’re gripping the Kindle, wherever you put your thumb, it will self-detect a dead zone in the Cap touch. It will just readjust, and it’ll know that the finger is there,” Keith said. Alongside the bezel-free redesign, the standard six-inch Kindle is now 6.8 millimeters thick and weighs 140 grams, making it both thinner and lighter than its predecessor. Amazon is positioning it as the most pocket-friendly Kindle in the lineup. Amazon said the new display is also 30% faster at page turns than the previous generation. The lineup also introduces new colors, including Ube, Alpine Sky, Seaglass Green, Graphite, and Fig. The new Kindle starts at $149.99 and is available in Ube and Graphite. For the first time, Amazon is also offering an aluminum-backed version, with 32GB of storage and color options, including Alpine Sky and Seaglass Green. The redesign extends to the Kindle Paperwhite, which is also thinner and lighter than the previous generation. Amazon describes the Paperwhite as having the largest display in the Kindle lineup, along with the highest contrast ratio. The company says the combination is designed to deliver “deep blacks and crisp text, and images that pop off the screen, whether you’re reading in bright sunlight or under the covers at night.” The standard Paperwhite comes with 16GB of storage and costs $199.99 in Graphite. A 32GB Signature Edition costs $249.99 and is available in Graphite and Seaglass Green. The Kindle Colorsoft, which Amazon introduced in 2024 as its first Kindle with a color display, also adopts the thinner, lighter, flush-front design used across the refreshed lineup. The standard Colorsoft has 16GB of storage and starts at $289.99 in Graphite. A 32GB Signature Edition is available in Graphite and Fig for $319.99. The new Kindle and its aluminum version are available starting today in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Brazil, the U.K., Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Sweden, Poland, Japan, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Egypt, and Australia.

articles.title: Hearing tech startup Legato launches its AI hearing glasses | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The glasses stem from the startup’s goal of making hearing care more accessible by addressing the cost, comfort, and stigma associated with traditional hearing aids.
articles.body_text: Hearing tech startup Legato announced on Thursday that its flagship AI-based hearing glasses are now available for purchase. The glasses, called Legato Frames , integrate the company’s patented hearing-assistance technology into the arms of eyewear frames. Starting at $999, Legato Frames are designed for adults with up to moderate levels of hearing loss. The glasses stem from the startup’s goal of making hearing care more accessible by addressing the cost, comfort, and stigma associated with traditional hearing aids. Unlike traditional hearing aids, which often use directional microphones to focus on sounds coming from a particular direction and can struggle in noisy environments, Legato takes a different approach. Its AI-powered system distinguishes voices from background noise and amplifies voices while reducing unwanted sounds. While the frames have an open-ear design, sound isn’t broadcast to people around you. The frames feature a dual-speaker system that directs sound toward the wearer while canceling sound that escapes, reducing sound by 99% just a few inches away from the ear. All processing happens directly on the glasses, with no cameras or recording, the company says. The glasses weigh 34 grams with lenses and offer 10-12 hours of battery life. Legato Frames are available in three styles and support prescription lenses and Bluetooth streaming for music and calls. The official launch of the glasses comes a few weeks after the startup emerged from stealth with $12 million in funding from Neotribe Ventures, Listen, and Village Global. Legato was founded in 2024 by Mehul Trivedi and Steve Romine, who bring deep experience in wearables and hearing care from Bose, where Trivedi led the creation of Bose Frames and Romine ran the hearing aids division. After their time at Bose, Trivedi joined EssilorLuxottica, where he led smart eyewear efforts and worked on the Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses, while Romine went on to serve as COO of hearing care company Audicus. The pair then joined forces to explore the intersection of hearing technology and smart eyewear. Legato Frames can be purchased on the startup’s website or through select eye care providers in the U.S., where they are eligible for coverage by vision insurance. articles.title: Satlyt, founded by a former Google and SpaceX product manager, raises $8M to run AI on satellites | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Satlyt wants to be the Android of orbital computing, offering open software that works on many companies' satellites, versus SpaceX's closed, all-in-one iPhone-style approach.
articles.body_text: The way Rama Afullo tells it, he saw orbital data centers coming. The Kenyan American engineer previously worked in Google’s cloud computing business before a brief stint at SpaceX’s Starlink communications network in 2024. His experiences convinced him that there was untapped potential for computers in space. “When I was at SpaceX, I tried to pitch this internally. They said no. When I was at Google, I tried to pitch this internally. They said no,” he tells TechCrunch. So he left SpaceX and co-founded Satlyt , a new company with headquarters in Sunnyvale, California, and Nairobi, to build software for satellites that he hopes will let many satellites share the work of large computing jobs in space. The company has raised an $8 million seed round, Afullo exclusively told TechCrunch. The timing looks good for him. SpaceX has since gone all-in on orbital data centers, and Satlyt’s software is set to launch Thursday on a SpaceX rocket alongside the first prototype for Google’s space data center effort, Project Suncatcher. Unlike SpaceX, Google, or startups like Starcloud and Cowboy Space Company, Satlyt isn’t planning to build its own spacecraft. Afullo’s team is building the software to operate AI models on satellites, comparing his approach to VMware and Snowflake — companies whose platforms let users run complex software without worrying about the underlying infrastructure. “The folks like SpaceX who are doing orbital data centers — if they are the iPhone, we’ll build Android as a horizontally integrated, open ecosystem,” he said. In other words, Satlyt wants to offer software that works across many companies’ satellites. Satlyt has already flown its software on two demonstration missions. The initial focus is finding operational efficiencies for spacecraft, which typically depend on flight controllers on the ground to solve any problems that arise. Sending data back to Earth, known as downlink, is expensive and often slow, so using AI to make decisions on the spacecraft can mean real savings, either when resolving anomalies or by processing sensor readings on the spacecraft instead of on the ground. Earlier this year, Satlyt deployed Google DeepMind’s Gemma AI model onboard a spacecraft operated by Momentus. The model cut the size of a transmission about onboard software errors by more than 60%, the kind of efficiency that Afullo says can save hundreds of thousands of dollars per satellite each year. This week’s launch will put Satlyt’s software to work onboard a spacecraft built by TakeMe2Space, an Indian startup that builds computing hardware for satellites. The mission involves three customers: NASA, which is paying the company to test protocols for cloud computing in space; Stellerian, a startup focused on space surveillance (tracking objects in orbit) that wants to test image processing workloads; and TakeMe2Space itself, to show the satellite can host other companies’ software. Right now, few high-powered GPUs are in orbit. For now, the most likely opportunity lies in the kinds of workloads Satlyt is working on. But the company’s next project is to show that it can create a shared computing system — a cloud — spanning two different satellites, which it expects to attempt next year. If successful, it will allow the company to build a true compute cloud in orbit as a third-party provider to spacecraft builders. The way to think about it is that we turn your satellite into a revenue-generating managed service,” Afullo said.

articles.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon, called its most powerful model yet | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Google has released its latest Gemini model, marketing it as a workhorse for coding and cybersecurity work.
articles.body_text: Google parent company Alphabet has launched Gemini 4 Argon, a new AI model built to handle a variety of tasks such as coding, research, and writing. But it’s cybersecurity that Gemini 4 Argon is supposed to have a particular knack for, according to Google. Argon is only being rolled out to a select group of the company’s cyber partners through its Fairwind Program, Google’s security initiative. The model was trained specifically for defensive cyber work, and the company says it can “autonomously find, validate, and patch critical software vulnerabilities.” Argon is also said to be good at coding and engineering, with the company noting that its own staff have already been using the model for their daily work, including debugging and codebase migrations. Google also touts Argon’s ability to parse visuals — whether that’s analyzing the contents of long videos or charts. “Built to sustain deep reasoning across complex, long-horizon workflows, Argon is fundamentally changing the way we work and build at Google,” the company said in a blog post Wednesday. Top AI labs have rushed to release increasingly powerful models, attempting to outdo each other even as those very same firms warn that AI could spin out of control. Not long ago, OpenAI released Astra — which it hailed as its best model yet. Earlier this year, Anthropic’s Fable was also released with similar rhetoric from the company. Firms have done their best to market their services as superior to their competitors. In its blog, Google claims that Argon scored significantly higher than OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic’s Fable and Opus models across a variety of AI benchmarks. It cites Vals — an increasingly popular AI benchmarking startup — to show that Argon is currently the leading model on the company’s AI model index. Once considered “ behind ” in the AI race, Google has recently enjoyed success with Gemini. The company announced in August that its app had over a billion users per month , a metric that makes it competitive with OpenAI, which also recently announced that ChatGPT had reached a billion monthly users. articles.title: Factory CEO just accused his VC board adviser of spying for Cognition | TechCrunch
articles.summary: VC Chris Degnan and former board adviser to Factory AI has taken a job as chief revenue officer for competitor Cognition -- and everyone is arguing on X about it.
articles.body_text: Matan Grinberg, co-founder and CEO of the AI coding startup Factory, said in a post on X on Wednesday that he fired VC Chris Degnan from his role as a board adviser. Grinberg alleges that Degnan shared confidential information with Factory’s biggest competitor, Cognition. Two hours after Grinberg’s post, Degnan announced on both X and LinkedIn that he had joined Cognition as its chief revenue officer. He also subsequently refuted Grinberg’s allegations, saying in a separate X post that he wasn’t fired but resigned when he told Grinberg he was taking the job. Degnan was Snowflake’s first sales hire and later spent 11 years as the data company’s chief revenue officer. For the past five months, he has been a partner with RPT Partners, a Newport Beach, California, investor in Factory. Degnan is also a go-to-market adviser to startups at the much bigger venture firm Iconiq , a role that dates back to October of last year. Three-year-old, San Francisco-based Factory is an agentic coding startup whose AI agents can carry out programming tasks largely on their own. The company raised $200 million at a $5 billion valuation this month from Khosla Ventures, Blackstone, Sequoia Capital, Insight Partners, and others. Its customers include Nvidia, Blackstone, Royal Bank of Canada, Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and T-Mobile. Grinberg said he sees Cognition, the maker of the Devin coding agent, as his biggest competitor. Cognition raised another $2 billion at a $48 billion valuation earlier this month , and counts Mercedes-Benz, NASA, Goldman Sachs, and Citi as customers. Grinberg said on X that Degnan had earlier acknowledged having a “casual” conversation with a Cognition executive but had assured Grinberg that he had no interest in working for the competitor. According to Grinberg, Degnan said he had “made too much money” and was “too lazy to go work for Cognition,” which Grinberg said he “trusted and believed.” On Monday, however, Degnan apparently disclosed that he had actually been in ongoing talks with Cognition. This caused Grinberg to grow concerned about how much confidential information Degnan had about Factory, and how much he had shared and might share in the future with his new employer. He says he fired Degnan as a board adviser on Tuesday, writing: For weeks, while he sat in our board meetings and advised our leadership team, he was also confiding with executives of our largest competitor. Chris was subject to confidentiality obligations in connection with his work with Factory. We do not know the extent of the information he shared, but it puts his timely questions about our product roadmap and what the parity gap involves into a new light. But Degnan disputes that account as well. He says the last Factory board meeting he attended was weeks before he had “ever spoken” to Cognition and that he hasn’t shared confidential information. Degnan also says that when he told Grinberg that he was resigning to take the role at Cognition, Grinberg offered him a full-time job at Factory, which he declined. Really disappointed to see this. Here are the facts: -You did not terminate me. I resigned from my advisor position on Monday and told you I was going to Cognition. In response, you asked me to consider a full time role at Factory. I told you I wasn’t interested. -You claim… Degnan’s post announcing his new job at Cognition doesn’t mention Factory. Very notably, it does say that RPT Partners and the firm’s managing partner, Chad Peets, will now be working with Cognition. “I am thrilled that Chad and the RPT team will be working closely with me in our pursuit of building a generational company,” Degnan wrote.
